newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to detail uses of empty satellite slots.
newsitem.headline: Canada to detail uses of empty satellite slots.

text.p: Canadian Industry Minister John Manley said on Tuesday he would outline detials of potential uses for Canada's empty satellite slots as early as Wednesday.
"I expect to make an announcement on potential applications for the use of Canada's satellite slots this week, possibly as early as tomorrow." Manley told reporters after a parliamentary session.

Manley said last week he would invite Canadian companies to bid for the two satellite slots after a plan by U.S.-based Telquest Ventures and Tele-Communications Inc failed to get approval from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission. Under the bid, the two satellites slots were to be owned and operated by Telesat Canada.
Telesat is owned by Alouette Telecommunications Ltd, which is 57 percent owned by BCE Inc. The rest is held by Canadian telephone companies and by Spar Aerospace Ltd.
Among potential bidders, Manley has mentioned Telesat and Shaw Comminications Inc.
